fatal_errors: The proposed intervention—adding atomically dispersed Pt—is not the target intervention, which was a closed-loop high-throughput composition-and-synthesis optimization campaign evaluated primarily after severe ageing.

The cited evidence does not directly establish that atomically dispersed Pt on the proposed near-equiatomic automotive alloy simultaneously survives relevant ageing, resists H2O/NO effects, and improves multicomponent exhaust conversion.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad activity, poisoning-resistance, PGM-use, and durability problem and proposes a testable paired comparison. It is nevertheless not a reconstruction of the target study. It omits automated synthesis, machine-learning/Bayesian selection, inverse analysis, the high-alkalinity/low-temperature synthesis window, and post-ageing electronic reconstruction involving Cu–Pt sites. Its conditions are vague and differ from the specified 900 °C lean/rich water-containing ageing and near-stoichiometric NO/CO/C3H6/i-C5H12 feed. The baseline is only the unmodified catalyst rather than the Pd benchmark and random-search baseline. Evidence E1 supports Pt nanoparticle stability on a high-entropy oxide, E2 supports CO-resistant single-atom Pt in another application, and E3 supports Pd single atoms in oxidation; collectively these make the alternative plausible but do not validate the full automotive claim or the asserted high-entropy anchoring mechanism. The experiment could falsify performance claims, but it needs exact feed composition, ageing protocol, replicates, statistical criteria, and species-resolved conversion measurements.
